title: Random Silicon Sampling: Simulating Human Sub-Population Opinion Using a Large Language Model Based on Group-Level Demographic Information
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the ability of language models to replicate the survey responses of different demographic subgroups on socio-political issues. One of the demographic variables used to define these subgroups was 'church attendance', which served as a proxy for religiosity. The paper measured the similarity (using KL-divergence and Chi-Square tests) between the model-generated response distributions and the actual survey responses from groups categorized as 'attend church' and 'do not attend church'.
findings: The language models showed a statistically significant difference in replicating the 2020 presidential voting choices of church attendees compared to actual survey data, indicating lower accuracy for this group. Across ten other socio-political topics, the models' ability to replicate opinions of church-goers was slightly less accurate (higher KL-divergence) than for non-church-goers, suggesting the models' inherent biases affect their performance in simulating opinions of religious individuals.
